screening.reason: Reports a diagnostic prediction (ASD vs. HC) analysis of ABIDE I resting-state fMRI functional connectivity using graph-theoretical features and an SVM, stratified into five age groups (Inclusion 2, 3).

evidence_spans.text: In this study, we used the fMRI data of 816 individuals enrolled in the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) to introduce a new biomarker extraction pipeline for ASD that relies on the use of graph theoretical metrics of fMRI-based functional connectivity to inform a support vector machine (SVM).
evidence_spans.claim: The study used fMRI data of 816 ABIDE individuals, extracting graph-theoretical metrics of functional connectivity to inform an SVM classifier.

evidence_spans.text: Our methodology achieved better results than most state-of-the-art investigations on this dataset with the best model for the >30 years age group achieving an accuracy, sensitivity, and speciﬁcity of 95, 97, and 95%, respectively.
evidence_spans.claim: The best model (>30 years age group) achieved 95% accuracy, 97% sensitivity and 95% specificity.

evidence_spans.text: we used the preprocessed version of ABIDE I (Di Martino et al., 2014) data publicly available via the Preprocessed Connectome Project (Cameron et al., 2013b). The preprocessing pipeline we used for this study is the Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes (CPAC) (Cameron et al., 2013a). Regions of interests (ROIs) were deﬁned as the 116 regions in the automatic anatomical labeling (AAL) atlas (Tzourio-Mazoyer et al., 2002).
evidence_spans.claim: Preprocessing used the CPAC pipeline via the Preprocessed Connectomes Project, with ROIs defined by the 116-region AAL atlas.

evidence_spans.text: Any subject that had a consistently 0 time-series was omitted from the dataset.
evidence_spans.claim: Subjects with a consistently zero time-series were excluded from the dataset.

evidence_spans.text: All Sites 109 342 190 137 51 816 Number of participants from each site for each age group as well as the overall number of participants in a site that were used for this study. Last row shows the total number of subjects in each age-range.
evidence_spans.claim: 816 subjects across 22 sites were distributed into five age ranges (5-10, 10-15, 15-20, 20-30, 30-65 years: 109, 342, 190, 137, 51 subjects respectively).

evidence_spans.text: We then use a sequential feature selection technique to choose the top 10 features that contribute to this classiﬁcation.
evidence_spans.claim: A sequential feature selection (wrapper) method chose the top 10 of 817 graph-theory features per network-extraction method for the SVM.

evidence_spans.text: We minimized the risk of overﬁtting by using three limiting approaches. First, the simplest kernel (linear) was used for the SVM. Second, only 10 features were used to learn to classify between 104 subjects. Finally, using 10-fold cross validation ensured the model is only evaluated on data points that it has not experienced before.
evidence_spans.claim: Overfitting was limited using a linear SVM kernel, only 10 selected features, and 10-fold cross-validation so the model was evaluated only on unseen data.

evidence_spans.text: The raw data supporting the conclusions of this manuscript will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation, to any qualiﬁed researcher.
evidence_spans.claim: Raw data will be made available by the authors to any qualified researcher on request, rather than openly deposited.

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort/site distribution, pipeline and atlas are explicit, and the authors describe deliberate overfitting-control steps (10-fold CV, a single linear kernel, only 10 features); the main uncertainty is whether the wrapper-based sequential feature selection was confined to the training folds, and no explicit site covariate or harmonisation is used across the pooled multi-site sample within each age group.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (SVM on graph-theoretical features) using ABIDE I resting-state fMRI, 816 individuals across 22 sites, stratified into five age groups (exact ASD/HC split reported only in a supplementary table).
narrative_row.methods: CPAC/PCP-preprocessed functional connectivity (AAL atlas, 116 ROIs; multiple connectivity measures) summarised into 817 graph-theoretical features, reduced to 10 via sequential feature selection and classified with a linear SVM per age group; evaluated via 10-fold CV with 10x10 Welch's t-test model comparisons (FDR-corrected).
narrative_row.outcomes: Best model (>30 years age group) achieved ~95% accuracy, 97% sensitivity, 95% specificity; centrality measures were the most consistently informative features across age groups.
narrative_row.key_limitations: ASD/HC split not available in the extracted full text (only in a supplementary table); no numeric motion/FD threshold reported; unclear whether feature selection was confined to training folds; no site covariate/harmonisation across the pooled multi-site sample; data available only on request, not openly deposited.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: An age-stratified ABIDE I analysis demonstrating that graph-theoretical centrality features combined with careful overfitting controls (linear kernel, few features, 10-fold CV) can achieve high accuracy in an older-age ASD subgroup, though feature-selection leakage risk is not fully resolved by the reported methods.

kg_link.cohort_description: 816 ABIDE I individuals across 22 sites, stratified into five age groups (5-10, 10-15, 15-20, 20-30, 30-65 years), after excluding subjects with a consistently zero time-series; exact ASD/HC split reported only in a supplementary table not captured in the extracted full text.
kg_link.pipeline: CPAC (Configurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes) via the Preprocessed Connectomes Project
kg_link.finding: Best model (>30 years age group) achieved ~95% accuracy, 97% sensitivity and 95% specificity using graph-theoretical centrality and other connectivity features with a linear SVM; centrality measures contributed most to classification across age groups.
evidence_quotes: All Sites 109 342 190 137 51 816 Number of participants from each site for each age group as well as the overall number of participants in a site that were used for this study. Last row shows the total number of subjects in each age-range.

Our methodology achieved better results than most state-of-the-art investigations on this dataset with the best model for the >30 years age group achieving an accuracy, sensitivity, and speciﬁcity of 95, 97, and 95%, respectively.

We minimized the risk of overﬁtting by using three limiting approaches. First, the simplest kernel (linear) was used for the SVM. Second, only 10 features were used to learn to classify between 104 subjects. Finally, using 10-fold cross validation ensured the model is only evaluated on data points that it has not experienced before.
